"Jason wants an easy life, but things just keep getting harder."

characters.bio: Jason Duval is a character due to appear as one of the protagonists in Grand Theft Auto VI. His voice actor is yet to be officially revealed.

p: Jason is a former Army serviceman who works for local drug runners in the Leonida Keys. He later becomes partners with Lucia Caminos, with the pair becoming involved in a criminal conspiracy spanning Leonida.
Brian Heder, a veteran of the Keys' drug trade, allows Jason to live rent-free at one of his properties in Key Lento in exchange for helping with local shakedowns.

Jason is partners with Lucia Caminos. Rockstar Games describes Lucia as the "engine" of their partnership and Jason as the "brake", with the two characters complementing one another and pushing and pulling each other throughout the story.

The pair function as the protagonists of Grand Theft Auto VI, with the player able to determine whether their relationship is platonic or romantic based on the Relationship System. The player can also switch which of the characters they are currently playing as, although some situations will require the player to play as Jason or Lucia. <!--

characters.bio: Lucia Caminos is one of the two protagonists in Grand Theft Auto VI. Lucia is the first major female protagonist in the the series to have a fully voiced role. p: Lucia is a criminal who was incarcerated at the Leonida Penitentiary after fighting for her family. After being released from prison, Lucia becomes partners with Jason Duval. She sees a life with Jason as a possible way out and is committed to changing the odds in her favor. <!--

He introduces them to the large-scale heists and criminal operations that become part of their story. Rockstar Games also intended Raul to embody Vice City and its local criminal culture.

Raul is seen in Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look when Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos pick him up while he is attempting to escape from the police. The pair help Raul escape the area, after which he tells them to "Keep their phone on," suggesting that Jason and Lucia are part of his crew.

characters.name: Jack Howitzer
characters.home: The Motor Motel, U.S. Route 68, Harmony, Blaine County, San Andreas
characters.bio: Jack Howitzer is a character appearing as a media personality in the of the the series.

p: Howitzer claims to have appeared in over 40 films before his prison stint. Howitzer's most notable role was as a war hero from Canyon Entertainment's action film Evacuator.
Jack Howitzer's earliest known film, Loincloth, was released in 1984. Throughout the 1980s, he appeared in the Evacuator sequel, titled Exploder: Evacuator Part II.

By the end of the 1980s, Howitzer's popularity had eventually declined and his career slowed down. He released Special Needs Cop in the 1990s, a severely politically incorrect film in which he endangers the lives of special needs children and other innocents. He also became delusional, believing that his movies were real and the Soviet Union could still attack (despite the fact they had collapsed in 1991).
In , the Weazel News website reveals that Howitzer instead served 15 years in prison for shooting a radio show host in the 1990s, was paroled by 2008, and was now set to have his own reality show.
Despite being paroled in 2008, sometime between 2008 and 2013, Jack was convicted of an unspecified crime which included aggressive driving and a police car chase, with Howitzer being sent to prison.

By 2013, Howitzer was finally released from Bolingbroke Penitentiary. He is still clearly disturbed and uses "Ho Chi Sock", a sock puppet dressed as an Asian, to cope with his situation, as well as continuing to believe that the 1980s aren't over. According to him, the mid '80s to the early 1990s was the greatest time in the history of America. Howitzer is seen living in a room at The Motor Motel and is being filmed as part of a reality show. In the show, a talent agent named Rufus Bellows is trying to talk Jack down from doing anything impulsive and to pitch a comeback film about Jack Howitzer, though apparently no one wants to be a part of it or make it, presumably because of Howitzer's current unpopularity, his mental and emotional instabilities, and because the script is apparently too dated for the present day.

As part of the show, Rufus gets Jack to set up Lifeinvader and Bleeter accounts, and Jack is seen posting a response to Moe Chinpoko who is trolling his page. Jack is then seen burning down Moe's house in Mirror Park.
Throughout Grand Theft Auto Online, reruns of his show continue to be played on TV.

In 2019, as part of The Diamond Casino & Resort update, the player can buy Howitzer's movie posters (Evacuator, Exploder: Evacuator Part II and Push-Up - The Movie) and props used by him to decorate their Master Penthouse.

In official video footage of Grand Theft Auto VI, a DVD copy of Exploder: Evacuator Part II can be seen being sold alongside other movies in a 24/7 store.
He has his own website in GTA V: JackHowitzer.com.

A howitzer is a type of artillery piece characterized by a relatively short barrel and the use of comparatively small propellant. The reference is explained by Howitzer's career in war films.
A pedestrian standing near a news stand in Algonquin states that Howitzer is getting his own reality show. He then says that Howitzer can suck Ho Chi's balls.
If the player startles a certain female pedestrian, she will say out loud "Jack Howitzer's ballsack!"

A Weazel News report mentions that Jack was jailed for shooting a radio host in the early 1990s. This is a reference to the previous incarnation of Jack Howitzer's character in the 3D Universe accidentally shooting Billy Dexter on Entertaining America in , although not revealing the name of the show or the radio host killed in the .
The reporter talks about Jack resurfacing after shooting a radio host in the early '90s, and then continues to talk about people's complaints with his new show.

Jack makes a reference to the television comedy, M*A*S*H, on his reality TV show. He is heard saying, "I never meant to kill that baby! I thought it was a chicken!", a nod to the emotional finale of M*A*S*H.

story.h: Events of Grand Theft Auto VI
p: In the mid-2020s, the criminal is arrested by the Vice-Dale Police Department. According to a Mega Noticias news report, one of his own tattoos served as self-incriminating evidence.

Following the release of the first trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI, Lawrence Sullivan demanded up to $2 million from Rockstar Games, claiming his likeness was used for the character in the trailer. "Florida Joker ain't having that," he said on his TikTok account, "y'all took my likeness, y’all took my life."

On December 13, Sullivan posted a video on TikTok with purple-dyed hair and wearing an orange prison jumpsuit to ape the character more closely and demanding $3 million from Rockstar Games – "I'm giving you the biggest free marketing you got in the entire history of running this GTA game," he said. "For that, I want an extra million dollars."

p: Macca the Gator is the titular character of a hit television show produced in Leonida. Rockstar Games describes the show as being popular across the state and uses the character as the inspiration for the Goodtime State – Vice City Collection of merchandise.

Macca is depicted as an anthropomorphic pink alligator wearing a blue shirt with palm tree patterns. A six-inch figurine of Macca is included in the Goodtime State – Vice City Collection. The figure depicts him smoking and holding a flamingo blood martini, and its base can be opened.

Macca also appears on a magnetic mirror included in the collection and on the front of a double-sided souvenir poster featuring characters from his television show. The reverse of the poster features a map of Leonida.

characters.bio: Méndez is a character in Grand Theft Auto VI. He is an officer of the Vice City Police Department who appears to have prior knowledge of Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos.

p: Méndez is an officer of the Vice City Police Department. He first appears in the second trailer, where he is shown during a police operation and tells other officers, “Us cops, we gotta protect each other.” In Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look, Méndez takes part in a police raid on a drug operation visited by Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. Jason and Lucia are at the location to collect a shipment when police arrive, leading to a shootout inside the building.

While attempting to escape in an elevator, Jason and Lucia discuss Méndez and whether he knows who they are. Méndez is subsequently seen shooting one of the armed occupants of the building and issuing orders to other officers. He begins to turn toward Jason and Lucia just as the elevator doors close.

p: Raymond is first seen in the Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look. He operates a drug lab inside a rundown apartment building in a district of Vice City, o where members of his crew are cooking and packaging drugs.

Jason and Lucia are sent to him to pick up drugs on Boobie Ike’s behalf, but Raymond is hesitant to move product after his partner Ernesto’s disappearance. Raymond reluctantly orders a gang member to complete the exchange anyway, only to get a call from Ernesto himself, who confesses that he snitched to the police. As a task force quickly breaches the building, Raymond takes up arms to join his gang in a shootout. Amid the chaos, Raymond directs Jason and Lucia to his aunt’s residence to escape through the window.

weapons.desc: The Hammer is a melee weapon appearing in , GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The weapon was intended to appear in and but was cut during the development of both titles.

p: The Hammer in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City has a red/black handle with a grey head. Tommy Vercetti will wield and use it in a similar manner to the Baseball Bat and the Nightstick.

The Hammer is the worst weapon in its class, being unable to knock the enemy down with a single hit unlike most other blunt weapons, while also knocking them out of its rather short range. It is, however, cheap, readily available and lightweight, although outclassed by the Screwdriver in every sense except for the fact it is able to smash cars.
The Hammer, along with the Screwdriver and the MP5, are the only weapons that do not have a spawn point in the city and have to be purchased.
Washington Beach, Vice Beach Available to buy from Bunch of Tools for $20.
North Point Mall, Vice Point, Vice Beach – Available to buy from Tooled Up for $20.
Little Havana, Vice City Mainland Available to buy from Screw This after completion of Phnom Penh '86 for $20.

weapons.name: Heavy Machine Gun
weapons.desc: The Heavy Machine Gun is, as the name implies, a heavy machine gun due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

weapons.name: Hunter Sniper
weapons.desc: The Hunter Sniper is a sniper rifle due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

weapons.name: Knife
weapons.desc: The Knife is a melee weapon appearing in almost every game in the 3D Universe and , and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is manufactured by Hawk & Little in GTA V.

weapons.name: Micro Submachine Gun
weapons.desc: The Micro Submachine Gun is a submachine gun due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

weapons.name: Molotov Cocktails
weapons.desc: Molotov Cocktails, or Molotovs, are thrown weapons appearing in every game since , and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Molotov cocktail is an incendiary weapon that is used to set a small area on fire. As in real life, molotovs are home made; they are prepared by inserting a rag into a partially filled glass bottle, allowing the rag to ignite the flammable liquid within. This causes the soaked rag to become flammable itself, allowing it to be lit on fire. Because the fumes from the flammable liquid (which are actually what catches fire, not the liquid itself) are contained within the bottle, full ignition does not occur until the glass container is broken, allowing the fumes to escape. This normally happens upon impact of the Molotov against a hard surface, after being thrown.
Unlike most weapons, the Molotov Cocktail in Grand Theft Auto 2 is one of the most basic weapons, as well as having a generic design of a bottle with the rag set on fire.

weapons.name: Mustang .357
weapons.desc: The Duke Arms Company Mustang .357 is a revolver due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The revolver can be seen held by a biker woman across her partner's chest in an official screenshot. The Duke Arms Company logo can be seen behind the cylinder, while "Mustang .357" can be seen engraved along the barrel.

weapons.name: Pistol
weapons.desc: The Pistol is a handgun that appears in GTA IV, , GTA V, GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is manufactured by Hawk & Little in GTA V and GTA Online.

p: The Pistol appears in every game in the , usually provided at the start of the game as the first weapon the player obtains. It is a reliable backup weapon, but not one that should be used as a primary, as it is outclassed by many other weapons in damage, fire rate, and overall effectiveness.

The Pistol was featured in Grand Theft Auto VIs Trailer 1 release artwork, seen being held by protagonist Jason Duval. It appears largely unchanged in influence and design from its GTA V counterpart, though notably without its Hawk & Little branding on the slide, implying the manufacturer may have been changed.

weapons.name: Polymer Pistol
weapons.desc: The Klose K17 is a pistol due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The pistol can be seen on the table Boobie Ike is sat at in an official screenshot. Lucia can also be seen holding one at her cheek in another screenshot, where the "9mm" caliber marking can be seen, along with a serial number (KL1701). This variant also lacks the front slide grip. Finally, Brian can be seen handing one over to Jason in another screenshot.
In the Ultimate Edition content web page, the pistol was named and a special engraved variant for Lucia was revealed, along with a special variant of the Girardi ES9 pistol for Lucia.

weapons.name: Pool Cue
weapons.desc: The Pool Cue is a tool and a weapon in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, The Lost and Damned and Grand Theft Auto Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: In The Lost and Damned, the Pool Cue is officially added as a weapon into the game, albeit as a halved version. Additionally, pool can still be played. There is also an own full-length cue added in the game, which appears to have better aspect, featuring the halved cue as the lower section of the full-length variation.

The Pool Cue performs similarly to the Baseball Bat, sharing the same damage (depending of the attack). However, the Pool Cue has no dodging animation, which only allows the player to block attacks and also makes it impossible to perform counter-attacks in a fight.

weapons.name: Rocket Launcher
weapons.desc: The Rocket Launcher (formerly named and frequently referred to as the RPG, standing for Rocket Propelled Grenade) is a rocket-propelled projectile weapon appearing in GTA IV, , GTA V, and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is manufactured by Shrewsbury in GTA V and GTA Online.

p: The RPG appears in every game in the , provided as a basic, albeit powerful explosive weapon. It is capable of massive destruction and power, with the ability to destroy nearly all vehicles and pedestrians. The weapon's name has changed numerous times throughout the :
In GTA VI, it is due to be named Rocket Launcher.

weapons.name: Smoke Grenade
weapons.desc: Smoke Grenades are thrown weapons due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

weapons.name: Speargun
weapons.desc: The Speargun is a projectile launcher due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

weapons.name: Beretta 92FS-inspired pistol
weapons.desc: The Girardi ES9 is a pistol due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Jason is seen firing the pistol from a car in the game's second trailer (1:50). He's also seen holding the pistol whilst sat on a motorcycle in an official screenshot.
In the Ultimate Edition content web page, the pistol was named and a special engraved variant for Jason was revealed, along with a special variant of the Klose K17 pistol for Lucia.

weapons.name: Bersa Thunder 380-inspired pistol
weapons.desc: A Bersa Thunder 380-inspired pistol is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The pistol can be seen in Lucia's hand as Jason closes the trunk of their car in a video on the promotional website. Lucia is also seen holding the same weapon in official artwork, where she is seen in the arms of Jason in a motel bedroom.
In the art cover the weapons seems to sport "Nipper 38" and "Made in Brazil" markings.

weapons.name: Capo pistol
weapons.desc: A Capo pistol is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Jason can be seen holding the pistol in a liquor store robbery with Lucia at the end of the game's first trailer (1:16). The pistol can also be seen in Raul Bautista's hand in an official screenshot, where he is seen inside a saloon car with a bag of cash on the passenger seat.

weapons.name: Double-barreled shotgun
weapons.desc: A double-barreled shotgun is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A poacher can be seen aiming the shotgun at an alligator off the side of his airboat in an official screenshot. It assumes the design of a double-barreled shotgun, as seen from the aerial shot.

weapons.name: Duke assault sniper rifle
weapons.desc: A Duke Arms Company assault sniper rifle is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A poacher is seen with an assault sniper rifle resting on his leg while on his airboat in an official screenshot. A Duke Army Company engraving can be seen above the magazine.

It appears to be a sniper rifle adaptation of the Duke carbine, both featuring almost identical stocks, magazines, and barrels, albeit with a longer one as opposed to the carbine's standard-length barrel.

weapons.name: Duke carbine
weapons.desc: A Duke Arms Company carbine is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Jason can be seen holding the carbine in an official screenshot. A Duke Army Company engraving can be seen above the magazine.

weapons.name: Duke special ops carbine
weapons.desc: A Duke Arms Company special ops carbine is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Raul Bautista can be seen using the carbine to hold off VCPD officers in a video on the promotional website. The weapon is similar in design to the Duke carbine but features a shorter barrel and a different stock.

weapons.name: Heckler & Koch MP5/40-inspired submachine gun
weapons.desc: A Heckler & Koch MP5/40-inspired submachine gun is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Lucia and Jason are both seen bearing the submachine gun in the game's second trailer (1:15), during a hostage situation.

weapons.name: Mini golf club
weapons.desc: A mini golf club is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Cal Hampton can be seen holding the mini golf club in an official screenshot. It is a metal putter with a blue plastic grip.

vehicles.name: 8F Drafter
vehicles.desc: The Obey 8F Drafter is a two-door coupe appearing in GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The rear of a black 8F Drafter can be distantly seen driving down a main thoroughfare in an official screenshot of Ambrosia.
The "Racing The Edge" livery is a reference to the iconic from Need for Speed: Most Wanted and Need for Speed: Carbon.

vehicles.name: Airboat 09
vehicles.desc: The Airgator Airboat 09 is an airboat due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The boat can be seen in two official screenshots of the Grassrivers, where they are being used for alligator hunting and fishing activities in the region. The same boat is also seen pursued by a Buzzard Attack Chopper in the second trailer (2:18).

vehicles.name: Aleutian
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Aleutian is a four-door SUV appearing in GTA Online as part of The Chop Shop update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A black Aleutian can briefly be seen at a parking lot in Port Gellhorn in the second trailer (2:28). Multiple instances of the Aleutian can also be seen parked at the Allied Crystal Sugar Refinery parking lot in the Ambrosia postcard featured on the game's promotional website.
Available for purchase from Legendary Motorsport for $1,835,000.
The glass and running light on the passenger side headlight of the vehicle were missing on its highest detail model, and were only visible on its LOD models.
This was fixed with the Bottom Dollar Bounties update.
The "Snorkels" customization category does not appear when customizing the car in the Executive Office Vehicle Workshop.
The "Chrome Grille" customization option is misspelled as "Chrome Grill".

vehicles.name: Alpha
vehicles.desc: The Albany Alpha is a 2-door sport coupé appearing in GTA V, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The Alpha previously appeared in the 3D Universe, also as a 2-door sport coupé.

vehicles.name: Alvino V1
vehicles.desc: The Principe Alvino V1 is a sport bike due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The motorcycle first appeared in an official screenshot of Jason Duval, where he is seen on a green Alvino V1 with a worn-out "#76" livery, holding a pistol.

vehicles.name: Arcturus
vehicles.desc: The Arcturus is a vehicle due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Asterope GZ
vehicles.desc: The Karin Asterope GZ is a four-door sedan appearing in GTA Online as part of The Chop Shop update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A white Asterope GZ can be distantly seen parked in Watson Bay in an official screenshot of the Grassrivers.

Several visual modifications available for the Asterope GZ take notable inspiration from different refresh cycles and trim levels seen on both Australian and North American versions of the XV30 Camry. In particular, the "Executive Grille" option takes after the XLE trim from the 2005–2006 model years, and the "Flared Skirt" option integrates elements from the optional ground effect body kit available for the SE trim.

vehicles.name: Astron
vehicles.desc: The Pfister Astron is a five-door compact SUV appearing in GTA Online as part of The Contract update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The rear of a black Astron can be seen storming through Port Gellhorn during a high-speed chase in the second trailer (2:29). An Astron can also be seen driving along Catalan Boulevard in an official screenshot of Vice City.
Available for purchase from Legendary Motorsport for $1,580,000.
An inaccessible red Astron belonging to Tanisha Jackson can usually be found parked outside 3671 Whispymound Drive with a custom plate "TAN1SHA".

vehicles.name: Avarus
vehicles.desc: The Liberty City Cycles Avarus is a chopper featured in Grand Theft Auto Online as part of the Bikers update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Bike Service This vehicle may be randomly selected to be serviced and returned to a customer.

vehicles.name: Baller

A blue one is seen in the opening shot, driving on a highway near the Leonida Penitentiary in Vice-Dale County (0:03).
Driving southbound on Interstate 97 ahead of a Towtruck (0:51).
A white one is seen parked up in a parking lot on the artificial islands between Vice City and Vice Beach (0:31).

vehicles.name: Banshee
vehicles.desc: The Bravado Banshee is a two-door sports car appearing in GTA IV, , , GTA V, GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The Banshee has appeared throughout the the series, returning from the 3D Universe. It shares its reputation with the Infernus for being one of the two longest running sports cars in the series.

p: Windows are unavailable if the "No Roof" modification is installed. :B Only available at Benny's Original Motor Works (enhanced version). :HSW Only available after a Hao's Special Works Performance Upgrade at the LS Car Meet (Expanded & Enhanced Editions).
It is sometimes found at Francis International Airport.
It often spawns around Alderney City, Middle Park, City Hall, Castle Gardens, The Exchange, Castle Garden City Algonquin, and Rotterdam Hill.
It sometimes spawns around Beachgate, Middle Park East, Hatton Gardens, Lancaster and Lancet.
It occasionally spawns around Varsity Heights, Westminster, The Meat Quarter, Suffolk, and South Slopes.
Final Destination Lenny Petrovic drives one as his getaway vehicle. The metal bars and the roof are combined with the seats. Occasionally, it may appear as a hybrid variant.
No. 1 Brucie's unique yellow and black Banshee appears in the starting cutscene.
Meltdown Niko chases Luca Silvestri's crew in a Banshee stolen from a man close by.
Exotic Exports The Banshee is one of the ten vehicles wanted by Brucie Kibbutz.

vehicles.name: Benson
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Benson is a box truck appearing in GTA IV, , GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The truck returns from the 3D Universe where it assumed the design of a much smaller box truck.

vehicles.name: Biff
vehicles.desc: The HVY Biff is a large multipurpose truck featured in GTA IV, GTA V, and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Two Biffs can be found in a construction site near Gainer Street in South Bohan, Bohan.
The Biff can usually be found driven round Acter Industrial Park in Alderney.
It can be seen driven on highways or freeways.
It can be commonly found in Pillbox Hill and La Puerta (enhanced version only).
Ivan the Not So Terrible A Biff can be seen blocking a street near the construction site where Ivan tries to escape.

Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend After getting ambushed, the diamonds are thrown into the back of a Biff.

A utility-focused Bison operated by Vice-Dale County can be seen in the game's second trailer, parked along Interstate 97 (0:35).

vehicles.name: Bison
vehicles.desc: The second generation of the Bravado Bison is a crew cab pickup truck due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A silver second generation Bison can be seen pulling a jet ski trailer in traffic along Interstate 97, in the game's second trailer (0:35). Later on, a red one can briefly be seen passing Lucia as she does her community service (1:27).

vehicles.name: Blazer
vehicles.desc: The Nagasaki Blazer is a quad bike appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Blazer's presence in Grand Theft Auto VI was first spotted in the game's first trailer, where it can be seen in a group of bikers driving through La Perle in Vice City (1:06).

vehicles.name: Blista Compact
vehicles.desc: The Dinka Blista Compact (also known as simply Blista) is a three-door hatchback appearing in GTA IV, , , GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The car returns from the 3D Universe where it also assumed the design of a hatchback.

vehicles.name: BMX
vehicles.desc: The PED Cycles BMX is a bicycle appearing in GTA V and GTA Online. The bike previously appeared in the 3D Universe where, in one appearance, it had two variants.

p: A missing poster for a grey BMX can be briefly seen on a bulletin board in the lobby of a Vice City apartment complex in the game's second trailer (1:43).

vehicles.name: Boat Trailer
vehicles.desc: The Boat Trailer is a towable trailer appearing in Grand Theft Auto V and Grand Theft Auto Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Boat Trailer's presence in Grand Theft Auto VI was first spotted in the game's first trailer, where a Bobcat XL can be seen in the opening shot towing a Boat Trailer with an unnamed bow rider motorboat mounted on it (0:02).

vehicles.name: Bobcat XL
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Bobcat XL is a two-door pickup truck appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Bobcat XL made its first official appearance in the opening shot of the game's first trailer, where it can be seen towing a Boat Trailer carrying a bow rider motorboat (0:02). It can later be seen in a parking lot on Vice City's artificial islands (0:31). In the second trailer, a closer shot of its rear with its tailgate down is briefly shown as Jason exits a grocery store (0:44). The Bobcat XL also appears in four official screenshots of Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Port Gellhorn, and Ambrosia.
In its official appearances, the Bobcat XL appears to have undergone minor design updates, including additional front vent windows, higher-quality taillight textures, and a redesigned rear bumper.

vehicles.name: Boxville
vehicles.desc: The Brute Boxville is a multi-stop truck appearing in GTA IV, GTA V, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A pink Boxville can be seen on the Ambrosia section of the game's promotional website.

vehicles.name: BTN Delmar
vehicles.desc: The BTN Delmar is a static container ship due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The ship is seen in the first trailer, docked at PortViceCity, while several speedboats race by (0:23).
Bilgeco, Jetsam, and Boxtrax containers are amongst the many seen on the ship.

vehicles.name: Buccaneer
vehicles.desc: The Albany Buccaneer is a two-door coupé appearing in GTA IV, , , GTA V, GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A white Buccaneer with a black vinyl roof and its driver-side door open can be seen parked on the double yellow centerlines of a road near an intersection in the Crosstown neighborhood of Vice City, behind a white Cypher and Dominator ASP, in the first trailer (0:45). The vehicle's custom lowrider variant also appeared in the first trailer.

vehicles.name: Buccaneer Custom
vehicles.desc: The Albany Buccaneer Custom is a two-door lowrider appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Buccaneer Custom can be seen parked behind a PMP 700 outside a car meet in the Stockyard neighborhood of Vice City, in the first trailer (0:27).

vehicles.name: Buffalo
vehicles.desc: The Bravado Buffalo is a four-door sedan appearing in , GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The car returns from the 3D Universe where it assumed the design of a two-door coupe.

p: The Buffalo's presence in Grand Theft Auto VI was first spotted in the game's first trailer, where a gray Buffalo can be seen during a street takeover in Crosstown (0:45). The Buffalo would later appear in two official screenshots of Vice CIty, particularly in Downtown and La Perle.
The Buffalo is equipped with a GPS system with a female voice, but only if the player leaves the "selected cars" (default) option in the audio menu.

vehicles.name: Buffalo STX
vehicles.desc: The Bravado Buffalo STX is a four-door sedan appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The top of the car is visible in the first trailer during a street takeover in Crosstown (0:46). The rear of the car can also be distantly seen in the first trailer ahead of the Tulip driven by Lucia and Jason as it passes the shopping mall in Waning Sands (1:00).
A police variant, displaying various police department liveries, also appears throughout the game's official media.
The "Sprunk Racing" livery is derived from the Sprunk Buffalo, with the racing number "68" retained from said vehicle.

vehicles.name: Buffalo STX Pursuit
vehicles.desc: The Bravado Buffalo STX Pursuit is a four-door police sedan in GTA Online as part of the A Safehouse in the Hills update on April 2, 2026, and also due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Buffalo STX Pursuit can be seen in the middle of an intersection in Vice City, along with two "interceptor" Police Cruisers; one VCPD and one VDPD, in the first trailer (1:07). It is depicted with a green and white Vice-Dale Police Department livery and is equipped with a blue/red LED lightbar.
The Vice-Dale Police Department livery seems to be based on that used on real-life .
The Vice Beach Police Department livery seems to be based on that used on real-life .

vehicles.name: Burrito
vehicles.desc: The first generation Declasse Burrito is a cargo van appearing in GTA IV, , , GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The van returns from the 3D Universe where it also assumed the design of a light cargo van.

p: The Burrito lineup serves as the basis for a wide array of vans, including cargo, passenger and cutaway designs. The vehicle also has a distinctive second generation model with a face lift design.

vehicles.name: Buzzard Attack Chopper
vehicles.desc: The Nagasaki Buzzard Attack Chopper (formerly named "Buzzard") is a light attack helicopter featured in , GTA V, GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Buzzard is evidently based on the AH-6, an attack variant of the MH-6 Little Bird light observation helicopter, with the tail similar to the MH-6's predecessors, the OH-6 Cayuse and the MD 500C. It also features a forward-looking infrared pod (FLIR) under the cabin, similar to the real-life AH/MH-6M Little Bird variant.

The vehicle is armed with miniguns that resemble the M134 Miniguns and are fed by a large ammo box on the rear bay, as well as additionally featuring rocket pods, each one loaded with eight rockets that resemble Hydra 70 unguided rockets.

Compared to the Maverick or the Annihilator, the Buzzard is depicted with a rather compact fuselage and a bubble glass canopy, having a curved front face with a small circular light on top and a large FLIR camera/searchlight pod, as well as curved side doors for the occupants. Around the middle/rear section, the aircraft has open sides that expose the rear bay, two small stub wings and short skids with tall struts, as well as an elevated section on top that partially surrounds the main rotor shaft, four small fins beside it and a large circular exhaust on the rear end of the fuselage. The tail boom is relatively small in comparison to most helicopters, having the tail rotor on the left and a single horizontal stabilizer on the right. The vehicle bears the registration "17 340" on the front, the sides of the upper section and the upper vertical stabilizer.

The interior of the cockpit denotes its small appearance, fitted with a small flight instrument panel on the center and visible rudder pedals, while a tall wall separates the front section from the rear bay. Despite the open rear bay, the aircraft cannot carry passengers on it.

The Buzzard that Luis obtained for Yusuf Amir was a prototype display model stolen from an arms deal. It was later repainted from black to gold by Yusuf – this difference would be first recognized during the mission Not So Fast, where Luis uses it to land on the roof of the Libertonian. The LCPD will call it a "black/gold helicopter" or "funny-looking helicopter", depending on which version Luis uses – the black Buzzard acquired by a cheat code or the gold Buzzard from Yusuf at the end of the game. The vehicle is also considered "illegal" in Liberty City.
The helicopter is only seen in a single primary color, being either the default black color or the special gold color.

vehicles.name: Caracara 4x4
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Caracara 4x4 is a four-door pick-up truck added to GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Caracara 4x4's presence in Grand Theft Auto VI was first spotted in the game's first trailer, where an orange model can be seen mud-crawling in the background at Thrillbilly Mud Club (0:55).
The Caracara 4x4 can then be seen multiple times in the second trailer and accompanying screenshots on the GTA VI Website, most notably as the vehicle of choice for Brian Heder.
The "Black Double Stripe" and "White Vapid Double Stripe" liveries are likely references to those of the Shelby F-150.
The "Rear Vapid Angle Stripes" livery pays a similar homage to the back stripes seen on the SVT Raptor.
The "Red Painted Scratches" livery seems to be based on the .
The "Painted US Flag" livery may be based on the .

vehicles.name: Carbon RS
vehicles.desc: The Nagasaki Carbon RS is a sport bike appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Carbonizzare
vehicles.desc: The Grotti Carbonizzare is a two-door grand tourer appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Carbonizzare's presence in Grand Theft Auto VI was first spotted in the game's first trailer, where a red Carbonizarre can be seen parked along an Ocean Drive-inspired road in Vice Beach (0:31).

The Carbonizzare appears in the first trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI, retaining most of its previous design, but with updated, higher-quality taillight textures and a subtly thicker, more conventional fender-to-taillight junction.

vehicles.name: Cheetah Classic
vehicles.desc: The Grotti Cheetah Classic is a sports car appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Chino
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Chino is a two-door coupé appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Chino would later be seen several times in the game's first trailer:
A black one can be seen trailing a blue Primo Custom, driving along the opposite side of the road near a car meet in the Stockyard neighborhood of Vice City (0:27).
Another black one can be seen parked behind two hustlers (0:30).
A red one can be seen stopped at an intersection during a street takeover in the Crosstown neighborhood of Vice City (0:45).

vehicles.name: Chino Custom
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Chino Custom is a custom coupe featured in GTA Online as part of the Lowriders update.

p: Can be converted from a standard Chino at Benny's Original Motor Works, for $180,000.
Grove Street Survival Used by attacking enemies.
Exotic Exports This is one of the hundred possible cars that can be requested by Brucie Kibbutz for delivery.

vehicles.name: Comet Retro Custom
vehicles.desc: The Pfister Comet Retro Custom is a custom sports car appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Comet Retro Custom appears stopped in the middle of an intersection in the first trailer (1:07).
The Tenshun livery is based on the Martini Porsche 911 RSR.

vehicles.name: Comet S2 Cabrio
vehicles.desc: The Pfister Comet S2 Cabrio is a two-door cabriolet appearing in GTA Online as part of The Contract update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The car can be seen in neon blue, parked up behind a Cheetah Classic along an Ocean Drive-inspired road in Vice Beach, in the first trailer (0:31).
A white Comet S2 Cabrio can then be seen driving through Vice Beach in a screenshot from the Vice City section of the game's promotional website.

The "Air Herler" livery is based on its one-off Group 5 variant, the 935/78 'Moby Dick', and by extension, the 2019 Porsche 935, a modern tribute to it.
The "Ron Racing" livery is based on the .

vehicles.name: Contender
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Contender is a pickup truck featured in Grand Theft Auto IV, returning in Grand Theft Auto Online as part of the Cunning Stunts update, released on July 26th, 2016, during the Cunning Stunts Bonuses II event, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Coquette
vehicles.desc: The Invetero Coquette is a sports car featured in GTA IV, GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Coquette D10
vehicles.desc: The Invetero Coquette D10 is a sports car appearing in Grand Theft Auto Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A blue Coquette D10 can be seen parked up behind a Landstalker XL along the Ocean Drive-inspired road in Vice Beach, in the first trailer (0:31).

A white Coquette D10 can then be seen parked along the same road in a screenshot from the Jason Duval section of the game's promotional website, while the rear of a blue one appears in Vice Beach in a screenshot from the Vice City section.
The 'Black Invetero Stripe' and 'Yellow Invetero Stripe' liveries may be influenced by the liveries sported by the Chevrolet Corvette C8.R during its many endurance race appearances.
The 'Paint Party' livery may be influenced by the "tie-dyed" Corvette C7 Z06 owned by YouTuber , which appeared at the Carlisle GM Nationals car show in 2016.

vehicles.name: Creado
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Creado is a two-door coupé utility due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Creado appears in the official artwork released alongside the game's first trailer, showing Lucia and Jason seated on its hood, with a Vapid logo visible on the grille.

It features prominently throughout the second trailer, where it appears to be showcased as the personal vehicle of Jason Duval. The name of the vehicle can be faintly made out on its front fender badges, most decipherable in a vertical, scroll-driven video of Lucia leaning out of its passenger window as it drives through Vice Beach on the mobile version of the game's promotional website.
Jason Duval The second trailer implies Jason owns a beater, turquoise Creado with a black-colored nearside fender.

vehicles.name: Cruiser
vehicles.desc: The PED Cycles Cruiser is a bike featured in Grand Theft Auto V and Grand Theft Auto Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Cypher
vehicles.desc: The Übermacht Cypher is a two-door sport compact car appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Cypher's presence in Grand Theft Auto VI was first spotted in first the game's first trailer, parked alongside other tuned vehicles during a street takeover in an intersection in the Crosstown neighborhood of Vice City (0:45). The door handles are now the primary color instead of black, and the taillights appear to have been updated, both differing from the car's previous rendition in GTA Online.
The "Team Xero" and "Redwood Stripes" liveries are both a nod to the iconic that commonly used on the M Series.
The former's design also takes inspiration from the Manhart MH2 GTR.
The latter's design resembles the livery seen on the fictional concept car.
The "Speed Demon" livery is a reference to the iconic from ' and '.

vehicles.name: Dashound
vehicles.desc: The Dashound is a coach appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: DF8-90
vehicles.desc: The Imponte DF8-90 is a four-door sedan appearing in GTA IV and , and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Dinghy
vehicles.desc: The Nagasaki Dinghy is a rigid inflatable appearing in GTA IV, , , GTA V, GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Dodo
vehicles.desc: The Mammoth Dodo is a seaplane appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The plane returns from the 3D Universe where it assumed the design of a conventional piston plane, thus making the HD Universe an interpretation of the 3D Universe's Skimmer (itself a variant of the Dodo).

p: The Dodo can be seen twice in the first trailer. It is first seen in the trailer's establishing shot (0:13), where it is seen towing a NINE1NINE banner. It is later seen swooping into view above the Leonida Keys in another aerial shot (0:34).
The Dodo can also be found throughout the game's second trailer and promotional website.

vehicles.name: Dominator
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Dominator is a two-door muscle car appearing in Grand Theft Auto V and Grand Theft Auto Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A red and black Dominator can be seen in the opening shot of the game's first trailer, traveling along a busy freeway in Hamlet near the Leonida Penitentiary.

vehicles.name: Dominator ASP
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Dominator ASP is a muscle car appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Dominator ASP's presence in Grand Theft Auto VI was first spotted in the game's first trailer, parked alongside other tuned vehicles during a street takeover in an intersection in the Crosstown neighborhood of Vice City (0:45).
The "Aggressor" front bumper options resemble an upside-down variant of that found on the Saleen S-281 Cobra.

vehicles.name: Dominator GT
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Dominator GT is a two-door convertible appearing in GTA Online as part of The Chop Shop update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A fully redesigned interior for the Dominator GT, identifiable by its A-pillar design, side mirror placement, soft-top roof, and the inclusion of the word "Dominator" on the speedometer, can be seen in an official screenshot of Ambrosia, where a man resembling Wyman is shown driving the car through a car wash. The interior also features what appears to be a functional infotainment system, with a touchscreen display identical to that of a four-door saloon shown in another official screenshot.

vehicles.name: Dominator GTX
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Dominator GTX is a muscle car appearing in Grand Theft Auto Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The car can be seen in white, driving along an Ocean Drive-inspired road in Vice Beach, in the first trailer (0:31).

vehicles.name: Dorado
vehicles.desc: The Bravado Dorado is a 4-door SUV appearing in GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A silver Dorado can be seen parked in Watson Bay in an official screenshot of the Grassrivers. It can also be seen in white driving past the Allied Crystal Sugar Refinery in the postcard video of Ambrosia on the game's promotional website.

vehicles.name: Double T
vehicles.desc: The Dinka Double-T (formerly stylized as Double T) is a sports bike appearing in , , GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A red Double-T can be partially seen parked next to a Carbon RS on an Ocean Drive-inspired road in Vice Beach during the game's first trailer (0:33).

vehicles.name: Dubsta
vehicles.desc: The Benefactor Dubsta is a four-door SUV in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Dubsta appears in the Port Gellhorn Pawn & Gun parking lot towards the end of the first trailer (1:10).

The Dubsta appears to have undergone a facelift, as seen in the first trailer, featuring a new front grille, badge, and front bumper inspired by the Mercedes-AMG G 65, while retaining the original light setup and general body shape from its previous iteration.

vehicles.name: Duster
vehicles.desc: The Western Company Duster is a fixed-wing airplane appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is the successor to the Cropduster from .

vehicles.name: Elegy Retro Custom
vehicles.desc: The Annis Elegy Retro Custom is a two-door sports car added to GTA Online as part of the Import/Export update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A green and a white Elegy Retro Custom can be seen parked at an intersection in the Crosstown neighborhood of Vice City, near a white Dominator ASP and a silver Penumbra, in the first trailer (0:45).
The "Not Tonight Pizzaboy" livery is an obvious reference to the quote "Street's closed, pizzaboy" from The Fast & The Furious, in which said scene featured a .
There's a small issue with the livery where the Device logo on the left skirt is upside down. This could be a developer oversight.
In a similar fashion, the "Midnight Racer" livery is an obvious nod to the famously driven by the late Paul Walker in 2 Fast 2 Furious.
The "Drift Missile" livery is a reference to , beater vehicles used as throwaway cars for drifting.
The "Low Spoiler" option is based on the .

vehicles.name: Emperor
vehicles.desc: The Albany Emperor is a four-door sedan appearing in GTA IV, , GTA V, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The car returns from the 3D Universe where it also assumed the design of a four-door sedan.

p: The Emperor can then be seen multiple times throughout the game's second trailer and official screenshots, now featuring updated badging and a new interior.

vehicles.name: Faggio
vehicles.desc: The Pegassi Faggio (pronounced FAH•jee•oh) is a compact scooter appearing in , GTA V, and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The Faggio previously appeared in the 3D Universe as a nearly identical model.

p: The rear of a white Faggio briefly appears in a scroll-driven animation of Jason and Lucia from the Grand Theft Auto VI's promotional website.

The scooter may spawn with exotic seat covers in purple velvet, or with leopard or zebra skin patterns. It also spawns in a variety of primary colours on the body and the handlebars, with the secondary one being applied in the form of dual stripes on the front panel and the rear end. It uses a set of plain rims with rivet details around, wrapped in medium-profile tyres.

vehicles.name: Feroci
vehicles.desc: The Bravado Feroci (pronounced as Ferochi) is a four-door sedan appearing in GTA IV and , and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: It also briefly appears in another clip, barely visible and in black, driving southbound along Route 2 past the Gas Stop branch in Port Gellhorn, several car lengths behind a two-door hardtop.
In both clips, the Feroci appears to have undergone several design changes.

vehicles.name: Freight Train
vehicles.desc: The Freight Train is a locomotive appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A blue and yellow Freight Train can be seen crossing a railroad bridge in an official screenshot of Mount Kalaga National Park. The train appears to sport a Boxtrax livery, with "Trax" visible on the engine compartment. It assumes a yellow and blue color scheme similar to that of The Bay Line and CSX locomotives operating in Florida.

vehicles.name: Furia
vehicles.desc: The Grotti Furia is a two-door supercar appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Furia appears driving westbound on Interstate 404 in Vice City in the first trailer (0:25). A man recording Lucia, who is standing out of the passenger seat of a tailing Zorrusso driven by Jason, can be seen leaning out of the Furia's passenger window. The front of the Furia can be seen later in the first trailer, parked on an Ocean Drive-inspired road along Vice Beach, behind a yellow two-door car (0:32).
A silver Furia can also be seen driving through Vice Beach in a screenshot from the Vice City section of the game's promotional website.
The "Masterpiece" livery is based on the displayed at the British Library's "Leonardo da Vinci: A Mind in Motion" exhibition.

vehicles.name: Futo
vehicles.desc: The Karin Futo (Japanese: フト) is a two-door sport compact car appearing in GTA IV, , GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A gray Futo later made an appearance in the first trailer, where it is shown to be stopped at an intersection in Vice City (1:06).
The "Karin Rally Team" and "Legendary Racer" liveries are based on Toyota yellow, orange and red racing liveries commonly used in the 70s and 80s in Autosport racing.
The "Team Auto Exotic" livery is based on the .
The "Rolling Dude No.7" livery available for the Futo is a homage to the "Rolling Guy" team from the Shutokō Battle (Tokyo Xtreme Racer in North America) series.
The "Garage Drift" livery is based on the .

vehicles.name: Gauntlet Classic Custom
vehicles.desc: The Bravado Gauntlet Classic Custom is a two-door modified muscle car appearing in GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A red Gauntlet Classic Custom can be seen parked near an intersection in Crosstown in the first trailer (0:45).
All ten livery options for the Gauntlet Classic Custom are derived from designs found on various Dodge Charger Daytona and Plymouth Superbird models:
"Stamped Bravado" - Stock livery on the 1970 Plymouth Superbird.
"White/Black/Red Gauntlet" - Stock livery on the 1969 Dodge Charger Daytona.
"No.36 Barracho" - Richard Petty's Superbird #43.

vehicles.name: Gauntlet Hellfire
vehicles.desc: The Bravado Gauntlet Hellfire is a muscle car appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The rear of an orange Gauntlet Hellfire can be seen driving along an Ocean Drive-inspired road in Vice Beach, in the first trailer (0:31). Later in the same trailer, a purple Gauntlet Hellfire with its passenger-side door open is shown parked near an intersection in the Crosstown neighborhood of Vice City (0:45).
In the second trailer, Jason Duval is seen shooting a pistol out of the passenger-side window of an orange Gauntlet Hellfire (1:50).

vehicles.name: Gauntlet Interceptor
vehicles.desc: The Bravado Gauntlet Interceptor is a two-door police muscle car appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Two instances of the Gauntlet Interceptor can be seen attending the scene of an overturned Vapid SUV on a busy Leonida highway in the first trailer (1:04).

The vehicle is operated by a highway patrol agency, with a black and tan two-tone livery seemingly based on that of the Florida Highway Patrol. What appears to be the Seal of Leonida can be seen on the trunk, while on the front fenders are yellow markings. It features interior emergency lighting mounted above the front windshield and a traffic advisor lightbar on the rear parcel shelf.

vehicles.name: Granger
vehicles.desc: The Declasse Granger is a four-door full-size SUV featured in Grand Theft Auto V and Grand Theft Auto Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Granger 3600LX
vehicles.desc: The Declasse Granger 3600LX is a four-door full-size SUV added to Grand Theft Auto Online as part of The Contract update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The design of the SUV in Grand Theft Auto VI appears mostly unchanged. However, there are notable modifications at the rear: a handle has been added to the trunk door, situated within the license plate space, which now has a dedicated holder. The arrangement of the rear lights has been modified, with the rear turn signals and reversing lights switching positions. The texture of the lights and the rear window glass has been updated. Additionally, a crease now runs in line with the reversing lights on the trunk. The twin exhaust setup has undergone changes, now featuring a single exhaust exit on the left side, positioned behind the rear bumper.

The Declasse badge placed above the license plate has been updated, featuring a new chrome/black winged variant of the original logo. The previously unused "3500 LX" badge has also been placed on the passenger side of the rear trunk door.

vehicles.name: Growler
vehicles.desc: The Pfister Growler is a two-door sports car added to GTA Online as part of the continuation of the Los Santos Tuners update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The "Vandal" and "Reverse Vandal" liveries are based on the .
The "Tinkle Sprint" livery is loosely based on the or .
The "Tamarro Racing" livery is inspired by the .
In the second trailer, the Growler features a redesigned front bumper and slightly different C-pillar influenced by the Porsche 992 GT3.

vehicles.name: Hellion
vehicles.desc: The Annis Hellion is a two-door SUV appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The truck can be seen in traffic on a busy Vice City freeway in the first trailer (1:03). It can then be seen in the parking lot outside Port Gellhorn Pawn & Gun, where Lucia and Jason flee in a Tulip (1:10).

vehicles.name: Impaler SZ
vehicles.desc: The Declasse Impaler SZ is a four-door sedan appearing in GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Infernus Classic
vehicles.desc: The Pegassi Infernus Classic is a two-door classic sports car appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A small portion of the rear of the car can be seen in front of a parked Landstalker XL, and behind a Granger 3600LX, along an Ocean Drive-inspired road in Vice Beach, during the first trailer (0:31).

vehicles.name: Ingot
vehicles.desc: The Vulcar Ingot is a station wagon featured in GTA IV, , GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Intruder
vehicles.desc: The Karin Intruder is a four-door sedan appearing in GTA IV, , GTA V, GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The car returns from the 3D Universe where it assumed the design of a compact sedan.

p: The Intruder can later be seen on a number of occasions within the first trailer, with notable changes in design:

A red model can be seen driving along a road with a girl twerking on the roof while being filmed by a passenger in a car alongside; this shot reveals its trunk and taillights. It also reveals a detailed, colored interior and chrome and plastic details around the side windows. A Karin badge can also be made out on the trunk face (0:44).
A second model, in silver, can be seen in traffic on a busy Leonida highway, where an overturned SUV can be seen (1:03).

A final model, also in silver, can be seen turning at an intersection in Vice City, where VCPD have stopped traffic due to a mob of bikers. In this shot, the entire rear quarter of the car can be seen (1:07).

vehicles.name: Itali GTO
vehicles.desc: The Grotti Itali GTO is a two-door grand tourer added to GTA Online as part of the continuation of the Arena War update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The Itali GTO has appeared throughout the the series, returning from the 2D Universe.

p: The Itali GTO's presence in Grand Theft Auto VI was first spotted in the game's first trailer, where a green GTO can be seen parked in the distance during the opening establishing shot of Vice Beach (0:11).
Can be purchased from Legendary Motorsport for $1,965,000.
Could be purchased from the Luxury Autos Showroom during SM722 Week.

vehicles.name: Jet
vehicles.desc: The Jet is a wide-body airliner appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Journey II
vehicles.desc: The Zirconium Journey II is a full-size RV featured in Grand Theft Auto Online as part of the Los Santos Drug Wars update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A beige Journey II can be partially seen parked in Watson Bay in a screenshot from the Grassrivers section of the game's .
Dax's Journey II can be requested as a transportation vehicle by calling him.

vehicles.name: Jubilee
vehicles.desc: The Enus Jubilee is a luxury four-door SUV appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Jubilee's presence in Grand Theft Auto VI was first seen in the game's first trailer, where it can be seen with its rear hatch open, parked on the curb of a street in the Stockyard neighborhood in Vice City (0:27).

vehicles.name: Jugular
vehicles.desc: The Ocelot Jugular is a four-door sports saloon appearing in GTA Online as part of the The Diamond Casino & Resort, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The car returns from the where it assumed the design of a two-door coupe.

p: The Jugular can be seen parked on the opposite side of the road along the Ocean Drive-inspired road in Vice Beach, facing oncoming traffic, in the first trailer (0:32).

vehicles.name: Kamacho
vehicles.desc: The Canis Kamacho is an off-road utility truck featured in GTA Online as part of The Doomsday Heist update, released on February 6th, 2018, during the Battle Week event, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The rear of a Kamacho can be distantly seen driving across a Vice City bridge in official artwork of Jason and Lucia.
The "Go Fast Fade" livery resembles the one found on the 1979 and 1980 Jeep J-10 Honcho.

vehicles.name: Landstalker XL
vehicles.desc: The Dundreary Landstalker XL is a full-size four-door SUV appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Later in the trailer, the rear of another Landstalker XL, in black, briefly appears as it drives past a flipped-over SUV on a Vice City highway (1:03).
The Landstalker XL can then be seen multiple times in the second trailer, where it is depicted with an updated grille.

The Mammatus is inspired by various Cessna aircraft, including the 172 Skyhawk, 177 Cardinal and 182 Skylane.

vehicles.name: Manchez
vehicles.desc: The Manchez is a dirtbike featured in , GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is manufactured by Maibatsu in the HD Universe.

p: A pair of Manchezes can be seen driving through muddy terrain in a screenshot from the Mount Kalaga National Park section of the game's promotional website.

vehicles.name: Marquis
vehicles.desc: The Marquis is a sailboat that appears in , , , GTA IV, GTA V, and GTA Online, and is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is manufactured by Dinka in the .

p: The Marquis can be seen in the waters of Leonida in the game's first trailer (0:31, 0:36) and in the Vice City and Leonida Keys postcards on the game's promotional website. It can also be seen stored on land next to Jason Duval's stilt house in the second trailer (0:21) and in the Port Gellhorn postcard.

The HD Universe rendition of the Marquis is based on , seen heavily in both the bow and the stern of the yacht, as well as the quarterdeck. The prow of the Marquis is not as long as the Adjutor, but the side rear windows and portholes are almost identical in shape.

vehicles.name: Maverick
vehicles.desc: The Maverick is a two and four-bladed helicopter appearing in GTA IV, , GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The helicopter is manufactured by Western Company in GTA IV and Buckingham in GTA V. The Maverick returns from the 3D Universe where it also assumed a design based on that of the Bell 206 family of helicopters.

vehicles.name: Mesa
vehicles.desc: The Canis Mesa is a four-door SUV appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The Mesa previously appeared in the 3D Universe as a two-door SUV of similar styling.

p: A red Mesa can be seen driving along the Keys Causeway in an official screenshot of the Leonida Keys.

vehicles.name: Minivan
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Minivan is a four-door minivan in GTA IV, GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Compared to its previous iterations, the Minivan appears to have undergone several design changes, improving its overall model quality. These enhancements include refined pillar and roof trim details, remodeled pull-bar door handles, redesigned wheels featuring red brake calipers and the Vapid emblem on the center cap, sleeker side skirts, and possibly new cabin seating.

vehicles.desc: The 4-axle variant of the HVY Mixer is a large cement mixer appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.desc: The Mule is a box truck that appeared in every game after , with the exception of and . It is manufactured by Maibatsu in the .

p: The Mule resembles a fifth-generation 1985–1987 Mitsubishi Fuso Canter, more specifically the FB433 model, as evident by the double, circular headlights, ridge on the doors following the headlights, and overall appearance, as well as the 1990s Mitsubishi Fuso Fighter/FM series, with some additional styling cues from the fifth-generation Isuzu Elf N-Series and the fourth-generation Hino Ranger.

vehicles.name: Nimbus
vehicles.desc: The Buckingham Nimbus is a private jet added to GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Nimbus' presence in Grand Theft Auto VI was first spotted in the game's first trailer, where it can be seen flying in the distance over Vice Beach (0:21).

Upon being converted into a personal aircraft, the Nimbus can be repainted with a primary color and a secondary color. It is possible to change the third stripe via the pearlescent color given with the primary "metallic" color. However, due to the second stripe using the plane's "wheel" (color slot 4) color, the color of the stripe cannot be changed.

vehicles.desc: The Lampadati Novak is a high-end crossover SUV featured in GTA Online as part of the continuation of The Diamond Casino & Resort update, released on November 7, 2019, during the Novak Week event, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

A heavily customized Outlaw is also visible driving along Vice-Dale County Road 561 in La Perle in an official screenshot of Vice City.

vehicles.name: Paragon R
vehicles.desc: The Enus Paragon R is a two-door grand tourer appearing in GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A black Paragon R can be seen driving at night along the Ocean Drive-inspired road in Vice Beach, in a scroll-driven animation of Jason and Lucia from the game's promotional website. It features a license plate that appears to be inspired by the current design used in the U.S. state of Arizona.
The Paragon R can also be seen twice in the background of two other screenshots on the game's promotional website, in the Vice City section.

The "Digital Sprunk" livery is loosely based on the .
