vehicles.desc: The Maibatsu Penumbra is a two-door coupé appearing in GTA V and GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A silver Penumbra can be seen in the first trailer, parked sideways near an intersection in the Crosstown neighborhood of Vice City, in front of a purple Gauntlet Hellfire (0:45).
The "Almost Had You" livery is based on Brian's from the movie '.

vehicles.name: Phantom
vehicles.desc: The Jobuilt Phantom is a tractor trailer truck appearing in GTA IV, GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Phantom Custom
vehicles.desc: The Jobuilt Phantom Custom is a semi-truck appearing in Grand Theft Auto Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Phantom Custom performs similarly to the Phantom Wedge, but having the same mass as the regular Phantom, resulting in a slightly better acceleration (which can be improved further with performance upgrades). The heavy mass gives the truck good traction on most surfaces, and is able to push most vehicles with no significant speed/torque loss. However, the brakes of the vehicle are somewhat lacking compared to other performance stats, requiring long distances before stopping the vehicle completely. When going on a downhill, the truck may take too much distance to stop, therefore it is advised to take great care when going downhill with the Mobile Operations Center attached.

Overall, it performs similarly to the Hauler Custom, but has limited steering capabilities in favour of mass and ramming power. Because of the open windows, the front occupants can make use of thrown weapons, such as Sticky Bombs and Proximity Mines. Players in the rear section can make use of two-handed weapons (namely Carbine Rifles and Combat MGs), at the cost of being vulnerable to fall from the truck if it flips down or being hit by another vehicle.

The Phantom Custom has, according to badges, a 24-valve Supercharged engine. Strangely, the engine model for the Phantom Custom appears to use 8 spark plugs textures, suggesting it is a petrol engine (untypical for a vehicle of this kind). It also suggests the engine can only be a petrol single-cam V8, but with a boxy appearance and connected to an adjacent air filter, with no sight of a supercharged as claimed. The engine sound is very different from other trucks, being a low-revving diesel engine also shared with the Hauler Custom.

stats.Capacity: 5 (driver, cab passenger and three external passengers)

vehicles.name: Phoenix
vehicles.desc: The Imponte Phoenix is a two-door muscle car appearing in GTA V, GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The Phoenix has appeared throughout the the series, returning from the 3D Universe.

p: The rear of a white Phoenix briefly appears in the first trailer, driving past a flipped-over SUV on a Vice City highway (1:03).

Grand Theft Auto VI's iteration of the Phoenix features several small, but notable design changes compared to its GTA V and Online rendition, most notably featuring large front fender vents, a new lower grille with high-beam lights, a cowl induction hood bulge by default, and a large hood decal reminiscent of the Firebird decal present on the Firebird Trans Am.

vehicles.name: PMP 700
vehicles.desc: The Schyster PMP 700 is a four-door sedan due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The car can be seen parked up at the side of the road amongst other customized cars in the first trailer (0:28). It is implied to be customized for a lowrider meet (with a pinstripe livery, custom wheels and stickers on the windshield). The rear of the car, with its "700" badge and "PMP" license plate, is seen later (1:08).
Another PMP 700 can also be seen in the same trailer (0:30), orange in color and having no modifications added.
Another green PMP 700 is seen in the distance, in a short video of Raul Bautista, on the game's promotional website.

vehicles.name: Police Cruiser
vehicles.desc: The Bravado Police Cruiser is a police car available in multiplayer modes of The Ballad of Gay Tony, appearing in Grand Theft Auto V, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The vehicle is a Bravado Buffalo similar to the first and second generation Dodge Charger Pursuit used by the New York Police Department. The livery is almost exactly the same as those used on the .

In-game, it is a police variant of the Buffalo, which is used by the LCPD, and uses almost the same features and liveries as the original Police Cruiser and Police Patrol. It is the third Buffalo-based vehicle featured, derived from the original FIB Buffalo.

Unlike other LSPD vehicles, the Police Buffalo does not have a two-digit number on the roof. It is, however, the only one having a badge painted on the hood. Sometimes, a version with a low-level spoiler attached sometimes spawns as well.

vehicles.name: Police Cruiser
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Police Cruiser, commonly referred to by the community as the Interceptor, is a law enforcement sedan appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: In Grand Theft Auto VI, the Police Cruiser retains its primary Ford Police Interceptor Sedan influence, though the front and rear fascias were redesigned to be closely aligned to its real-life counterpart. The outline of the C-pillar trim panel now appears to be inspired by the C-pillar quarter window of the ninth-generation Chevrolet Impala.

vehicles.name: Police Maverick
vehicles.desc: The Police Maverick (also known as simply Polmav) is a police helicopter appearing in GTA IV, , , GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is manufactured by Western Company in GTA IV and Buckingham in GTA V. The Police Maverick previously appeared in the 3D Universe where it also assumed the design of a standard Maverick with an appropriate police livery. From GTA V, the Police Maverick is no longer based on the standard Maverick and assumes a more modern design.

vehicles.name: Police Riot
vehicles.desc: The Brute Police Riot is an armored truck appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Police Riot appears in the second trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI, seen pursuing Jason and Lucia alongside two VDPD cars, shortly before Lucia fires a grenade launcher at them.

stats.Capacity: 8 (driver, 3 passengers and 4 passengers hanging on the sides)

vehicles.name: Primo
vehicles.desc: The Albany Primo is a four-door midsize sedan appearing in GTA IV, , GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The vehicle returns from the 3D Universe where it also assumed the design of a four-door midsize sedan.

p: The rear of a Primo can be partially seen driving along an Ocean Drive-inspired road in Vice Beach, in the first trailer (0:31). Its front end is then partially visible in an official screenshot of Ambrosia, where it is parked near a Xero gas station.

vehicles.name: Primo Custom
vehicles.desc: The Albany Primo Custom is a four-door lowrider appearing in Grand Theft Auto Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Primo Custom can be seen in blue, driving along the opposite side of the road near a car meet in the Stockyard neighborhood of Vice City, in the first trailer (0:27).

vehicles.name: Rancher
vehicles.desc: The Declasse Rancher is a two-door pickup truck appearing in GTA IV and , and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The vehicle returns from the 3D Universe where it also assumed the design of a two-door SUV.

p: The rear of the Rancher then appeared officially in the second trailer, shown driving down Interstate 97 in Vice City with two men sitting in its bed (0:35). It can also be seen parked next to a Blista Compact in the postcard for Port Gellhorn on the game's promotional website.

The overall design of the Rancher appears to have notably changed in Grand Theft Auto VI; with adjustments being made to the detailing of the vehicle. The rear bumper has been slightly updated and now holds the license plate for the vehicle as opposed to it being mounted on the rear tailgate. The taillights appear to have been redesigned, more closely resembling the taillights seen on the Rancher XL in GTA V. Other detailing updates include new body-colored wheel arches and an updated secondary color stripe design.

vehicles.name: Rebel
vehicles.desc: The Karin Rebel is a two-door pickup truck featured in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Across the three clips, the Rebel has seemingly undergone a multitude of design changes.
The Rebel later made its first official appearance in a screenshot on the Grassrivers section of the game's promotional website, shown in beige driving through Watson Bay.

vehicles.name: Rebla GTS
vehicles.desc: The Übermacht Rebla GTS is a four-door SUV featured in GTA Online as part of The Diamond Casino Heist update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The "Roadster Grille" modification option bears a strong resemblance to BMW's signature kidney grille.
The "Aztec" livery seems to be inspired by the one found on a .
The "German Automotive" livery seems to be inspired by the one found on the .

vehicles.name: Regina
vehicles.desc: The Regina is a four-door station wagon which has appeared in , , , , GTA V and GTA Online, and is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is manufactured by Dundreary in the .

p: In the HD Universe, the Regina's overall body design and greenhouse are now based on the older 1966–1970 Caprice Estate Wagon while also taking influence from a mix of the 1964 Pontiac Tempest Safari and the 1959 Pontiac Catalina in the front fascia design. The rear is mostly an original design, with cues from the 1968–1972 Chevrolet Chevelle/Malibu Wagon. The wheels take inspiration from 1960s GM rally wheels.

vehicles.name: Riata Classic
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Riata Classic is a vehicle due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Rolls-Royce Cullinan-inspired car
vehicles.desc: The Rolls-Royce Cullinan-inspired SUV is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It can be seen in the first trailer (0:28).

vehicles.name: Rubble
vehicles.desc: The Jobuilt Rubble is a dump truck appearing in Grand Theft Auto V and Grand Theft Auto Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Ruiner
vehicles.desc: The Imponte Ruiner is a three-door liftback appearing in GTA IV, GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The tail lights and trunk spoiler are shaped like those of the Camaro, but the area between and below the tail lights better resembles the Firebird, with badging positioned where the Firebird logo would be. Ruiners may feature "RUINER" decals and stripes along the lower part of the doors, much like those of the Camaro IROC-Z, although the stripes and decals share colors with the ground effects, much like the 1982–1984 Trans Ams.

vehicles.name: Rumpo Custom
vehicles.desc: The Bravado Rumpo Custom is a modified off-road van added to GTA Online as part of the Further Adventures in Finance and Felony update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: S23
vehicles.desc: The Lure Predator S23 is a bay boat due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The boat can be seen docked at a jetty where Jason and Lucia are sat, in the second trailer (1:21). The boat is later seen cruising down a canal in Vice City towards the end of the trailer (2:33). Two of the boats can also be seen side-by-side in the Leonida Keys, in an official screenshot, and another two docked in the Leonida Keys in a postcard.

vehicles.name: Sabre Turbo
vehicles.desc: The Declasse Sabre Turbo, also known as the Sabre GT, is a two-door muscle car appearing in GTA IV, , , GTA V, GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The Sabre Turbo has appeared throughout the the series, returning from the 3D Universe.

vehicles.name: Sadler
vehicles.desc: The Sadler is a pickup truck featured in , GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is manufactured by Vapid in the HD Universe.

p: The LOD model of a black Sadler also appeared prominently in a temporarily uploaded demo reel from a former Rockstar Toronto character animator in late 2025, which included a split-screen clip showing two angles of a female NPC in an in-game test-bed environment, with the Boardwalk Hotel visible in the background, stepping off the Sadler with unique animations: the left angle from its truck bed, and the right angle from its roof.

vehicles.name: Sanchez
vehicles.desc: The Sanchez is a dirtbike appearing in almost every GTA title since , and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is manufactured by Maibatsu in the .

p: The Sanchez remains relatively unchanged in every game it appears in, having the same dirt-bike chassis design, off-road fittings and accessories, along with relatively similar performances. While not particularly fast compared to sport bikes such as the PCJ 600, the soft suspension, high ground clearance and very light weight makes it useful for stunt biking and off-road applications. They can be found on the streets of suburban or rural areas, and they are also sometimes used in the stadium(s) in and , as part of side-missions.

vehicles.name: Sanchez (livery)
vehicles.desc: The Maibatsu Sanchez (livery) (formerly Sanchez) is a dirtbike featured in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Vehicle does not have access to the regular Respray options. The only available options are the ones listed here. :** Vehicle is limited to Bulletproof Tires and Tire Smokes.

vehicles.name: Sandking XL
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Sandking XL is a lifted four-door pickup truck appearing in GTA V and GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Schafter LWB
vehicles.desc: The Benefactor Schafter LWB is a luxury four-door saloon appearing in GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Schafter V12
vehicles.desc: The Benefactor Schafter V12 is a luxury four-door sedan appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Scorcher
vehicles.desc: The PED Cycles Scorcher is a hardtail mountain bike appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A Scorcher can then be seen stood on tactile paving at a Vice City intersection in the first trailer (1:07).

vehicles.name: Sea Sparrow
vehicles.desc: The Sea Sparrow is a three-bladed amphibious utility helicopter appearing in GTA Online as part of the Southern San Andreas Super Sport Series update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The Sea Sparrow previously appeared in the 3D Universe where it also assumed the design of an amphibious variant of the in-universe Sparrow.

p: The Sea Sparrow can briefly be seen flying in the skies above Vice Beach in the first trailer (0:22). It can also briefly be seen flying above Vice Beach in the second trailer (0:38).

vehicles.name: Seashark
vehicles.desc: The Speedophile Seashark is a personal watercraft appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A red Seashark can be seen stationary by the shore of a crowded Vice Beach in the first trailer, positioned next to a yellow jet ski (0:22).

vehicles.name: Seashark
vehicles.desc: The second generation of the Speedophile Seashark is a jet ski due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Jason and Lucia can be seen speeding past party-goers on the Seashark in the game's second trailer (2:20). Two can also be seen being ridden on in the Leonida Keys in an official screenshot. In comparison to the first generation model, the second generation Seashark assumes a more angular design.

vehicles.name: Shamal
vehicles.desc: The Shamal is a multi-role jet-plane in and a regional jet in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is manufactured by Buckingham in the HD Universe. Similar business jets also makes multiple appearances in other Grand Theft Auto games, although they are uncontrollable and are only used as props.

p: A Shamal can be seen flying over the Vice City Sign at Vice City International Airport in a screenshot from the Vice City section of the game's promotional website.

vehicles.name: Sheriff SUV
vehicles.desc: The Declasse Sheriff SUV is a law enforcement vehicle appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

stats.Capacity: 8 (driver, 3 passengers and 4 passengers hanging on the sides)

vehicles.name: Slamvan
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Slamvan is a two-door pickup truck appearing in GTA V as part of the Festive Surprise update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The truck returns from the 3D Universe where it also assumed the design of a two-door pickup truck, albeit more modern in design.

vehicles.name: Speedo
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Speedo is a cargo delivery van appearing in GTA IV, GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Speedo resembles a 2006–2010 Chevrolet Express cargo van, with the frontal elements and the rear bumper taken from the 2003–2007 Ford E-Series, with the tail lights potentially inspired by the ones seen on GM's GMT400 platform trucks.

vehicles.name: Squalo
vehicles.desc: The Squalo is a cabin cruiser appearing in GTA IV, , GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is manufactured by Grotti in GTA IV and Shitzu in GTA V. The boat returns from the 3D Universe where it assumed the design of a speedboat.

p: The boat is seen numerous times in the game's second trailer and in official screenshots:
Two of the boats are seen outside Brian's Boat Works & Marina mounted on boat trailers in the game's second trailer.
A Squalo is seen in the Leonida Keys in an official screenshot.
A Squalo is depicted (and named) on an advertising billboard in an official screenshot.

vehicles.name: Stanier
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Stanier is a four-door sedan appearing GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The vehicle's design is largely similar to its prior renditions; however, changes have been made to the chrome and plastic trims, taillights, interior, and rims, which now feature Vapid emblems. The car also now includes a third brake light behind the rear window.

vehicles.name: Stratum
vehicles.desc: The Zirconium Stratum is a four-door station wagon appearing in GTA IV, , GTA V, GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The Stratum has appeared throughout the the series, returning from the 3D Universe.

p: The rear of a Stratum can be distantly seen in the opening shot of the game's first trailer, traveling along a busy freeway in Hamlet near the Leonida Penitentiary.

vehicles.name: Street Blazer
vehicles.desc: The Nagasaki Street Blazer is a modified quad bike added to GTA Online as part of the Bikers update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Bike Service This vehicle may be randomly selected to be serviced and returned to a customer.

vehicles.name: Sugoi
vehicles.desc: The Dinka Sugoi (Japanese: すごい; English: Amazing) is a five-door hatchback appearing in Grand Theft Auto Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A blue Sugoi can be seen parked in Watson Bay in a screenshot from the Grassrivers section of the game's promotional website, while the side of a gray one appears in Vice Beach in a screenshot from the Vice City section.

Two pre-modified variants of the Sugoi can be chosen as getaway vehicles to steal for The Diamond Casino Heist. They are one of the four sets of vehicles driver Taliana Martinez randomly allocates for the player.

vehicles.name: Sultan
vehicles.desc: The Karin Sultan is a four-door sports saloon appearing GTA IV, , GTA V, GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. The car also appeared in the 3D Universe, where it assumed the design of a mid-size saloon.

p: A green Sultan can be seen parked with its passenger-side door open, alongside other sporty vehicles, during a street takeover in an intersection in the Crosstown neighborhood of Vice City in the first trailer (0:45). The rear of a blue Sultan can later be seen driving past a flipped-over SUV on a Vice City highway (1:03).
A red Sultan is also visible in Vice Beach in a screenshot from the Vice City section of the game's promotional website.

vehicles.name: SuperVolito
vehicles.desc: The Buckingham SuperVolito is a helicopter appearing in Grand Theft Auto Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The SuperVolito can briefly be seen flying in the skies above Vice Beach, Vice-Dale County, in the first trailer (0:22).

vehicles.name: Swift
vehicles.desc: The Swift is a luxury four-bladed helicopter appearing in , in GTA V as part of The San Andreas Flight School Update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is manufactured by Maibatsu in TBOGT and Buckingham in .

p: A Swift can be seen flying over the skies of Vice Beach in an official screenshot labeled under Vice City.
The Santo Capra livery featured in TBoGT is inspired by the .

The Swift is considered a private shuttle helicopter with a long fuselage, which also makes use of marvellous aerodynamics, living up to its name. The aircraft has an angular nose with a relatively large cockpit, access doors for the pilot and copilot, and a nose landing gear. The main section features an open bay with relatively ample space (though unable to carry passengers), a tall engine compartment with a four-bladed main rotor and numerous intakes, along with side extensions that house the main landing gear and dual exhausts. The tail boom is slightly angled upwards and has small fins on the horizontal stabilizers, a four-bladed tail rotor on the right, and a strike guard on the lower vertical stabilizer. The interior features a small flight instrument panel with the corresponding control sticks and pedals.

The aircraft only spawns in a white primary colour for the fuselage and the tail boom, a secondary colour for the engine compartment, lower rear portion, part of the tail boom and the fins, and a blue pearlescent colour, together with a Santo Capro livery. It uses a set of industrial wheels derived from trucks such as the Benson, Mule and Phantom.

vehicles.name: Tailgater
vehicles.desc: The Obey Tailgater is a four-door saloon appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Tempesta
vehicles.desc: The Pegassi Tempesta is a two-door supercar featured in GTA Online as part of the Import/Export update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Can be bought from Legendary Motorsport for $1,329,000.
A yellow Tempesta can be one of the vehicles found randomly inside The Diamond Casino & Resort public parking garage, as such it will also be locked from the player.
Repo - Burn Rate Many examples have been torched by gang members and the players need to extinguish the car fires.
Casino Work: Under the Influence Can appear in this mission, where it must be delivered to the Casino while the protagonist is under the influence of alcohol.

vehicles.name: Toros
vehicles.desc: The Pegassi Toros is a four-door SUV appearing in GTA Online as part of the continuation of the Arena War update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Tow Truck
vehicles.desc: The Vapid Tow Truck (also and formerly named Towtruck) is a tow truck appearing in GTA V and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The Tow Truck can be seen in the game's first trailer (0:51). The truck is seen passing a "Leonida Man" dancing at the side of the freeway next to his Ruiner.

vehicles.name: Trailer (container)
vehicles.desc: The container/curtain-side variant of the Trailer is a towable trailer appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Trailer (flatbed)
vehicles.desc: The Trailer is a towable trailer appearing in GTA V, GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Trailer (tanker)
vehicles.desc: The Trailer is a towable tanker trailer appearing in GTA V and GTA Online, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI. It is manufactured (or used) by Brute.

vehicles.name: Transgressor
vehicles.desc: The Transgressor is a vehicle due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Tulip
vehicles.desc: The Declasse Tulip is a four-door muscle car appearing in GTA Online and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The car makes a noteworthy appearance in the game's first trailer, particularly towards the end, where it is seen involved in a getaway (1:00) and fleeing from Port Gellhorn Pawn & Gun (1:10), both involving Lucia and Jason. It can also be seen driving off into the sunset between a series of artificial islands near Vice City in the final shot of the second trailer (2:33).

vehicles.name: Tulip M-100
vehicles.desc: The Declasse Tulip M-100 is a two-door muscle car featured in Grand Theft Auto Online as part of the Los Santos Drug Wars update, and due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The rear of a black Tulip M-100 can be seen on a major thoroughfare, ahead of a pack of Final Chapter MC motorcyclists, in an official screenshot of Ambrosia. The vehicle's custom hi-riser variant previously appeared in the game's first trailer.
The "M-100 Stripes" liveries are based on the one for the of the 1980 Chevrolet Malibu Coupe.

The "Declasse Racing Stripes" liveries are seem to be inspired from the striped decals found on the Chevrolet Yenko , specifically the one for the 1970 Yenko "Deuce" Nova that the Vamos' "White Side Stripes" livery is primarily based on.
The "Two Tone Fade" livery is based on the decals on several Chevrolet Malibu Classic models, including the and the .
The "Hotring Throwback" livery is based on a near-identical variant of the Hotring Racer in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.

vehicles.name: '55 Vapid Stanier
vehicles.desc: The 1955 Vapid Stanier is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The car can be seen in yellow and white, parked up outside the Boardwalk Hotel along the Ocean-Drive inspired road in Vice Beach, in the first trailer (0:31).

vehicles.name: 1959 Cadillac-inspired car
vehicles.desc: A 1959 Cadillac-inspired car is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: A beater variant of the car is seen in the game's second trailer (0:21), where it is parked up behind Brian Heder's Caracara 4x4 outside of Jason Duval's stilt house.

vehicles.name: 6x6 conversion van
vehicles.desc: A 6x6 conversion van is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

vehicles.name: Audi Q7-inspired SUV
vehicles.desc: An Audi Q7-inspired SUV is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The SUV is seen twice in the first trailer:
On the freeway in the first scene of the trailer (0:03)

vehicles.name: Azimut 85-inspired yacht
vehicles.desc: An Azimut 85-inspired yacht is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The yacht can be seen among the artificial islands of Vice-Dale County in the distance in the game's first trailer (0:31). Party-goers can be seen standing on the yacht in the second trailer (1:23). It also appears again among the aforementioned artificial islands in the postcard video of Vice City on the game's promotional website.

vehicles.name: Azimut Atlantis 45-inspired yacht
vehicles.desc: An Azimut Atlantis 45-inspired yacht is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Party-goers can be seen standing on the yacht as Jason and Lucia speed past on a Seashark in the game's second trailer (2:20). A close-up of the bow of the yacht can be seen in an official screenshot, where it is anchored in the Leonida Keys.

vehicles.name: Benefactor saloon
vehicles.desc: A Benefactor saloon is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The car can be seen driving along a main throughfare in Vice Beach, in the game's second trailer.
It is depicted as a slab car with a candy red paintjob and Swangas rims. A Benefactor badge can be seen on the grille.

vehicles.name: Bison police truck
vehicles.desc: A Bravado Bison police truck is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The police truck can be seen in the middle of a street in Vice City in an official screenshot. A VDPD officer and two VCPD officers are seen apprehending a suspect nearby.

The truck assumes the design of a second generation Bison, also due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI, but with a lightbar, and depicted in what appears to be a Vice-Dale Police Department livery, made apparent by the presence of a gold emblem on the hood and doors, and faint green stripes along the sides of the vehicle).

vehicles.name: Boat trailer
vehicles.desc: A boat trailer is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The trailer can be seen coupled up to a lifeguard truck on Vice Beach in the first trailer (0:23).

vehicles.name: Box trailer
vehicles.desc: A box trailer is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The trailer can be seen with a Patriot Beer livery, being towed by a Phantom Custom, in the first scene of the first trailer (0:03).

vehicles.name: Bravado dually pickup truck
vehicles.desc: A Bravado dually pickup truck is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The pickup truck can be seen in red, parked up at an Arrow gas station in Leonard County, in the first trailer (0:50). The rear of the pickup truck can later be seen dragging a safe in the second trailer.

The vehicle takes up the design of a 4-door crew-cab pickup truck with large rear arches in dually configuration (a term used to denote pickup trucks that have dual rear wheel configuration). In the first trailer, it appears to be coupled up to a towable boat trailer with an airboat mounted on it.

vehicles.name: Bravado minivan
vehicles.desc: A Bravado minivan is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The minivan can be seen turning out of an intersection, whilst a group of outlaw dirt bikers flee from police, in the first trailer (1:07).
A taxicab variant of the minivan, with a yellow livery and roof sign, also appears throughout the game's official media.

vehicles.name: Bravado minivan taxi
vehicles.desc: A Bravado minivan taxi is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The vehicle can be seen driving down the Ocean Drive-inspired road in Vice Beach at night, in a scroll-driven animation of Jason and Lucia from the game's promotional website. The rear of the vehicle can be seen driving away in an official screenshot of Vice Beach labeled under Vice City. A Bravado badge can be seen on its grille.

vehicles.name: Bravado monster truck
vehicles.desc: A Bravado monster truck is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The truck is first seen in the background at Thrillbilly Mud Club in the game's first trailer (0:55). It can later be seen outside Delights in Port Gellhorn in an official screenshot.
It assumes the design of a Bravado pickup truck but with a higher ride height and large tires. <!--

vehicles.name: Bravado pickup truck
vehicles.desc: A Bravado pickup truck is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The truck can be seen in five scenes throughout the first trailer (0:25, 0:52, 1:07, 1:08 and 1:16) and in a scene of the second trailer (1:54). It also appears in the postcard video for Port Gellhorn on the game's promotional website.

vehicles.name: Brute excavator
vehicles.desc: A Brute excavator is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The vehicle assumes the design of a tracked excavator and features a large boom with a grappler attachment on the stick, a left-mounted driver's cab and an engine bay with exhaust stack. It sports a red paintjob and bears what appears to be the Brute logo on the boom, indicating the vehicle's manufacturer.

vehicles.name: Buick Reatta-inspired convertible
vehicles.desc: A Buick Reatta-inspired convertible is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The convertible can be seen driven by Lucia during a high-speed chase through Port Gellhorn in the second trailer (2:28).

vehicles.name: Buick Skylark-inspired car
vehicles.desc: A Buick Skylark-inspired car is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The sedan later officially appeared in the first trailer, seen parked up at a gas pump at an Arrow gas station in Leonard County (0:50). The rear of the car is also partially visible in a screenshot from the Ambrosia section of the game's promotional website.

vehicles.name: Burrito shuttle bus
vehicles.desc: A Declasse Burrito shuttle bus is due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The minibus can be be seen in white, driving along a busy freeway in the opening scene of the first trailer (0:03). Another one can be seen much further down the freeway in the distance. The bus reappears in the game's second trailer, where it is seen driving ahead of a red and white Rancher on Interstate 97 (0:35).

The local Final Chapter MC biker gang also wields considerable influence in the region.

In the mid-2020s, the city is holding a local mayoral election, with candidate Erin Henshaw seemingly leading in popularity. Their campaign is backed by Allied Crystal, whose logo appears directly on political yard signs alongside the slogan "the sweet lifeblood of Ambrosia", underscoring the company's deep influence over the city's politics.

locations.name: Mount Kalaga National Park

quotes.text:
WILD, WILD COUNTRY

Room to breathe on the state's northern fringes.

A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government.
quotes.src: Grand Theft Auto VI website.

locations.desc: Mount Kalaga National Park is a national park located on the northern border of the State of Leonida, due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Mount Kalaga National Park's natural formations generally consist of rugged forests, canyons and riverways. Hobbies and pastimes in the park include fishing, kayaking, hunting, and offroad racing. The national park hosts wildlife such as deer, cougars, and foxes.
The region represents the northernmost portion of Leonida, bordering the State of Gloriana, with the state line referred to in-game as the Leonida-Gloriana line.

The surrounding area features a variety of rural and outdoor environments, including ATV trails, mud parks, mountain bike trails, agricultural farms, high-end ranches, and a private golf course. The coastline also features beaches and coastal sand dunes, with bass fishing among the recreational activities available in the northern part of Leonida.

locations.name: Grassrivers

quotes.text:
WELCOME TO THE WETLANDS

The untamable jewel of Leonida’s crown.

You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves.

locations.desc: The Grassrivers is a natural region of flooded grasslands in Leonida, due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The wetland region is located in the southern portion of the State of Leonida, and is currently known to run through Vice-Dale County and Mariana County.

It was first indirectly referenced in GTA IV on Leftover-vacations.com in a Vice City travel advertisement, and on Craplist.net by a tourist who smuggled a crocodile from Vice City's wetland border to Liberty City.

locations.name: Leonida Keys
locations.desc: The Leonida Keys is an archipelago in southern Mariana County, Leonida, due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The keys consist of a series of tropical islands off the southern coast of Leonida, bordered by the Gulf of Mexico and the straits of Leonida, forming the southernmost part of the continental United States.
The keys are situated in Mariana County, accessible via the Keys Causeway in southern Vice-Dale County, with the route extending in an arc south-southwest and then westward.
Hurricane Roxy is implied to have impacted the region prior to the events of the game.

locations.name: Port Gellhorn

quotes.text:
LIVE HARD

This is Leonida’s forgotten coast.

Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. Jump on a dirt bike and hold onto your wallet.
quotes.src: Description on the GTA VI website.

locations.desc: Port Gellhorn is a city in Kelly County, Leonida, due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: The city appears to be a vast coastal area on the western side of Leonida, with a wide variety of commercial and industrial infrastructure interspersed with dense forests, open grassy fields, and rolling hills.
Port Gellhorn reappeared toward the end of the second trailer, offering another glimpse of its landmarks, including the Crossroad Park Minimall and the Bocamar Bridge.

Additional official screenshots and a postcard featured in a dedicated section for Port Gellhorn on the game's promotional website further highlight points of interest such as the Delights strip club and the city's seaport area.
The city is described by Rockstar as representing Florida's smaller and, in some cases, struggling tourist-trap areas, with abandoned attractions, cheap motels, and derelict strip malls.

The area surrounding Port Gellhorn features extensive countryside and recreational spaces, including forests, agricultural land, ranches, coastal dunes, beaches, and lakes. Activities available in the surrounding region include off-road driving, motocross, mountain biking, fishing, and destruction derby racing.

locations.name: Vice City

quotes.text:
EVERYTHING IN EXCESS

We're a long way from the '80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America.

The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world.

quotes.text: 1980s - The decade gets lost in a glorious debauched snowstorm of cocaine, neon and pastels as everyone seeks to emulate a Vice City lifestyle.
quotes.src: The Proposition 208 website's timeline in Grand Theft Auto V.

locations.desc: The City of Vice, commonly known as Vice City or simply Vice and often abbreviated as V.C., is a major city due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI, located in Leonida. The city also serves as the county seat of Vice-Dale County.

p: Vice City is a coastal metropolis located in the southeastern portion of the State of Leonida in Vice-Dale County. The city was previously referenced multiple times throughout the .

It is the most populous and densely populated city in the State of Leonida, regarded as the sun-and-fun capital of the United States of America, and is well-known for its vibrant atmosphere from the 1980s, and its history as a narcotrafficking and money-laundering hub for various transnational criminal organizations. PortViceCity, the city's namesake seaport, is also considered the cruise ship capital of the world.

The city features congested roads, beaches, and a cruise ship port, while its surrounding metropolitan area encompasses a variety of neighborhoods and environments. Rockstar Games describes Vice City as having been rebuilt and expanded from its previous appearances, with the increased scale of Grand Theft Auto VI allowing for a denser and more detailed depiction of the city.

The city's mainland rests on the shores of a south Leonida bay, which contains several natural artificial barriers known as the Rialto Islands along with Starfish Island that separate it from the neighboring city of Vice Beach, itself considered part of the Vice City metropolitan area.
Vice City is one of the six primary regions of Leonida, alongside the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park.

<!--- The following list shows neighborhoods officially revealed in trailers for Grand Theft Auto VI. Some of the neighborhoods were previously established in the HD Universe canon in Grand Theft Auto IV.

Vice City is influenced by a diverse population from all around the world. The city itself is infamous for the drug wars of the 1980s, natural disasters due to its subtropical weather conditions, and its decently-sized skyline of glimmering skyscrapers and condominiums. The city's culture of excess in the 1980s came to define the decade, as people aimed to replicate a "Vice City lifestyle" through indulgence in cocaine, neon lights, and flashy trends.

Vice City's organized crime was predominantly fueled by the illegal trafficking of cocaine ever since the 1980s to the present day. During the late 2000s, major traffickers have smuggled in cocaine to Russian mobsters in Liberty City, particularly the now defunct Rascalov Mafiya. One of Dimitri Rascalov's men, Andriy Maximov, has been arrested after being caught with a boatload of cocaine brought from Vice City. Smugglers commonly use speedboats and narcosubs to get the drugs in and out of Leonida.
Like other metropolitan areas in the United States, crime in Vice City is localized to specific poorer neighborhoods and immigrant population towns such as La Perle and Little Cuba.

It is implied that Liberty City-based mobsters operate in Vice City and/or its surroundings, including the formerly appointed Gambetti Crime Family lead successor Sammy Bottino, who was wanted for murder by the Vice-Dale Police Department circa 2007.

Methamphetamine became popular in Vice City circa 2008, which has reportedly "destroyed the lives and businesses of cocaine dealers" in the city. At some point circa 2019, a weed-based drug named "Zombie" induced users into committing cannibalism.

locations.name: State of Leonida
locations.desc: The State of Leonida (pronounced lay-oh-NYE-duh) is a state located in the United States of America, due to appear in Grand Theft Auto VI.

p: Leonida is world-renowned for its beach resorts, amusement parks, warm and sunny climate, nautical recreation, and hosting the busiest port in the world. Attractions such as the cities of Vice Beach and Vice City are referenced throughout the series.
The state is also indirectly responsible for the moon landing conspiracy theorists, and the Leonida Man phenomenon on social media.

In Grand Theft Auto VI, Leonida is the largest map created by Rockstar Games to date, described by Rockstar as being approximately twice the size of San Andreas in GTA V. The state is designed to be denser, more detailed and more interactive, with a greater number of explorable interiors and a variety of environments, towns and rural areas.

Leonida is divided into six primary regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park. These regions are based on different aspects of Florida, ranging from the urban and coastal environments of Vice City to the wetlands of Grassrivers, the tourist attractions of Port Gellhorn, the industrial areas of Ambrosia, and the rural and mountainous environments of Mount Kalaga.
To date, only a handful of cities and towns have been revealed as part of Leonida—two of which, Vice City and Vice Beach, were previously mentioned by name in titles.

p.t: The story follows criminal duo Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, who become involved in a criminal conspiracy spanning the state of Leonida. The two form a romantic relationship and work together as criminals, with their partnership becoming central to the story.

Lucia is recently released from the Leonida Penitentiary after being imprisoned for fighting in defence of her family. Jason grew up around criminals and later served in the Army before becoming involved in the drug trade in the Leonida Keys. Meeting Lucia gives Jason an opportunity to pursue a different life, although the pair's criminal ambitions continue to draw them into dangerous situations.

After an easy score goes wrong, Jason and Lucia find themselves caught up in a wider criminal conspiracy that extends beyond Vice City and across Leonida. The pair are forced to rely on one another as they become increasingly involved with the state's criminal underworld.

During their crimes across the state, the pair meet various figures across Leonida, including Brian Heder, an old-school drug runner who allows Jason to live at one of his properties in the Leonida Keys, and Boobie Ike, a Vice City businessman whose interests include real estate, a strip club, and a recording studio. Other known associates and criminals include Cal Hampton, Dre'Quan Priest, Real Dimez, and Raul Bautista.

The game takes place across the State of Leonida, including Vice-Dale County, home to Vice City. Other known locations include Leonida Keys, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, Grassrivers, and Mount Kalaga National Park.

Grand Theft Auto VI’’, like previous entries, is an open-world action-adventure game in which players control Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as they carry out criminal activities across the State of Leonida. Gameplay combines traditional Grand Theft Auto mechanics with expanded systems for character interaction, vehicle theft, police identification, and exploration.

Jason and Lucia can both be controlled during gameplay. The player can switch between the two characters during certain situations, including while they are apart from one another. The Extended Look demonstrates the player switching between Jason and Lucia during gameplay, including a transition from Lucia BASE jumping to Jason elsewhere in Leonida.

Many older gameplay elements, such as going to Gyms, having various Safehouses, and Carjacking have been updated, as shown by the Extended Look and further detailed by Rockstar Games co-studio head Rob Nelson in interviews with IGN.

Jason and Lucia can participate in a variety of criminal activities throughout Leonida, including robberies, vehicle theft, and the collection of stolen goods. The Extended Look demonstrates the pair carrying out a drug pickup, robbing a store, escaping from the police, and providing security for a client at a private event.

Players can also interact with characters and objects outside of missions. The Extended Look shows Jason and Lucia interacting with other characters, entering buildings, preparing for social events, and carrying out activities throughout the open world.

The Wanted Level returns with an expanded system for police identification. Police can identify Jason and Lucia using characteristics including their clothing, appearance, vehicle, and whether they are together. The Wanted Level can reach six stars.

Players can alter factors that identify them to make it more difficult for police to locate them. This includes changing vehicles and using different clothing. Jason and Lucia can use disguises to alter their appearance during criminal activities. The Extended Look demonstrates the protagonists wearing different clothing and disguises during missions and other situations.

Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos each have a Criminal Profile that tracks how well they act during criminal activities. The system is intended to reflect the way the player approaches criminal activity rather than simply recording how many crimes they commit. Rob Nelson described it as being influenced by whether the player goes beyond what is necessary during a crime, particularly when this behaviour is repeated.

The Criminal Profile can therefore be affected by the player's actions both during and outside of missions. The Extended Look demonstrates the system responding to interactions in the world, like a positive response when petting a dog, while also showing separate profile information for Jason and Lucia.

The system is distinct from the Relationship System, which tracks the relationship between Jason and Lucia. The Criminal Profile instead reflects the player's approach to criminal activity and can develop differently for each protagonist.

The Relationship System allows Jason and Lucia to interact with one another in ways that reflect their relationship. The Extended Look demonstrates the pair spending time together, communicating during activities, and interacting as a couple.

The open world features a variety of recreational activities and locations outside of the main story. Confirmed activities shown so far include Basketball, Scuba Diving, Weightlifting, Kayaking, Base Jumps, and visiting a Strip Club.

The game also features a greater variety of interactions with non-playable characters. Jason and Lucia can interact with people encountered throughout Leonida, while some characters can be greeted or taunted.
Rockstar Games announced the game's two editions on June 24, 2026, with pre-orders beginning the following day. The two editions are:
Ultimate Edition – US$100/£90/€100, featuring additional digital content including clothes, stores, and more side missions.
Pre-orders of either version of the game, as well as purchases made before November 20, 2026, include one month of GTA+ and the Vintage Vice City Pack.
Note that only the Standard Edition comes with a code in a box, while both editions are sold digitally.

There's also the Grand Theft Auto VI: The Goodtime State – Vice City Collection, which is effectively the collector's edition of the game and has a retail price of $399.99 in the US and £349.99 in the UK. It does not include a copy of the game.
Rockstar Games has not officially announced an online multiplayer component for Grand Theft Auto VI. The game is currently described as a "single player experience" in promotional material.

During Take-Two Interactive's annual shareholder meeting on September 17, 2026, CEO Strauss Zelnick stated that the company had not announced an online version of Grand Theft Auto VI, adding that it would be premature to discuss its business model.

On September 18, 2026, Twitch CEO Dan Clancy stated that the multiplayer component of Grand Theft Auto VI would launch in 2027. Rockstar Games has not confirmed the existence or release date of the online component.
